title: Arrays & Collections: Indexing & Transformations
description: Master JavaScript arrays: zero-based indexing, length tracking, mutating operations (push, pop), and higher-order transformation methods (map, filter).

objectives.statement: Access and update array elements using zero-based numerical indexing and the length property.
Transform and filter array data using iteration and modern array methods (map, filter).

content.title: Working with Lists of Data
content.hook: From shopping cart items to social feed posts, modern apps deal with ordered collections of data. Arrays are the primary structure for holding multiple values in order.
content.context: An array is an ordered list. Items are accessed using zero-based indices (array[0] is the first item). Arrays come with built-in methods like .push() to add items, and .map() and .filter() to transform lists cleanly.
goals: Add and remove elements with .push() and .pop().
Transform arrays using .map() and filter items using .filter().

content.title: The Zero-Indexed Array Model
content.description: Array elements occupy continuous slots indexed from 0 to length - 1. array[0] holds the first item; array[array.length - 1] holds the final item.

content.prompt: What color will be printed to the console?
content.explanation: colors initially has 3 items. .push('yellow') adds 'yellow' to index 3, making length 4. colors[4 - 1] evaluates to colors[3], which is 'yellow'.

feedback.correct: Correct! .push() appended 'yellow' to the end, and colors[length - 1] reads the last element.
feedback.incorrect: Remember that .push() modifies the array by adding to the end, increasing length.

content.title: Filter and Format Lesson Scores
content.prompt: Given `const rawScores = [45, 80, 95, 60, 100];`, filter scores `>= 70` into `const passingScores`. Then map `passingScores` to create `const scoreLabels = passingScores.map(score => 'Score: ' + score);`.

feedback.correct: Awesome work! .filter() and .map() provide clean, declarative array transformation.
feedback.incorrect: Check that passingScores filters >= 70 and scoreLabels formats each item as 'Score: ' + score.

content.question: What is the numerical index of the very first element in any non-empty JavaScript array?

options.text: It depends on how the array was initialized

content.explanation: JavaScript arrays are strictly zero-indexed. The first item is always located at index 0.

feedback.correct: Correct! JavaScript arrays always start at index 0.
feedback.incorrect: Remember that indices are zero-based, meaning the initial element is at index 0.

content.title: Arrays & Collections Mastered
takeaways: Arrays store ordered lists accessible by 0-based index (array[0] is the first item).
.push() adds to the end; .length gives total item count.
.map() transforms every element into a new array; .filter() selects elements matching a test.
